purpose: Source inventory of every allowlisted scheduler module and event handler; this is not an authorization or RLS policy.

shared_boundary.database_identity: Scheduler and EventBus control-plane processes retain the configured runtime PG_USER and PG_PASSWORD. Child processes receive standard application settings, but worker-specific secrets are filtered unless an exact source-controlled mapping permits them. The sensor-anomaly handler and four cache handlers use dedicated worker database helpers without shared-DSN fallback; the two global notification handlers can opt into a separate notification-enqueue login. The NOI snapshot, current-weather, and weather-forecast modules use separately named worker DSNs, strip shared PostgreSQL settings from their children, and use exact secret mappings; other scheduled jobs and handlers still use the shared runtime database identity.
shared_boundary.signed_tenant_context: Migration 405 and services.common.tenant_context provide signed worker context. Scheduler dispatch and the EventBus parent do not establish it; the sensor-anomaly handler uses dedicated credentials and signed transaction context through migrations 405-414, and the four cache handlers use the shared dedicated cache_invalidation worker identity through migrations 415-416 when enabled. Migration 417 provides the global data_stale and threshold_breached enqueue handlers a separate exact login and bounded source-event validation, not tenant scope. Migrations 418-419 revoke inherited PUBLIC EXECUTE on mobile credential and worker-context functions; the runtime-role bootstrap restores only the exact runtime, worker, and bounded-owner grants. Migrations 425-427 add default-off signed location-scoped NOI snapshot, current-weather, and weather-forecast operations; other scheduled jobs and handlers remain outside these integrations.
shared_boundary.module_argument_validation: Static module-specific operation schemas validate command_args before schedule activation, run-now, generated job plans, scheduler-allowlisted code-owned job runs, and worker subprocess creation. Unsupported manual/destructive operations and source-less recurring sensor ingestion fail closed; existing task rows are not rewritten.
shared_boundary.deployment_effect: Inventory only; it does not change grants, activate schedules, or enable RLS.

scheduled_modules.scope: Legacy entrypoint retained for persisted task compatibility until schedule owners reconcile existing rows. New native JobSpecs use services.ingestion.weather_worker. Manual CLI calls must select one location or explicitly choose --all-locations; an omitted selection only prints help. The all-location query remains a code-level aggregate operation, not tenant authorization.
scheduled_modules.idempotency: Legacy weather_observation insert has no explicit conflict clause; ClickHouse projection is keyed by payload hash. A replay may create a second PostgreSQL observation.
scheduled_modules.retry_boundary: Legacy persisted-task retries may repeat provider reads and PostgreSQL inserts; no source watermark is recorded by this entrypoint. Reconcile legacy tasks before using this shared-identity path.

scheduled_modules.scope: Default-off native worker requires one explicit --location-id, receives only the exact worker DSN, worker credential, and OpenWeatherMap provider key, and establishes a signed weather_observation/ingest grant for the selected location before each database operation. Migration 427 exposes signed coordinate lookup and one bounded atomic observation/audit/outbox/receipt function; the worker has no direct application-table access.
scheduled_modules.idempotency: A transaction-scoped advisory lock serializes identical location/provider responses. The private receipt key is (location_id, provider_payload_hash); duplicate scheduler delivery returns the existing observation without repeating audit or projection effects. Observation, success audit, ClickHouse outbox intent, and receipt commit atomically.
scheduled_modules.retry_boundary: A retry repeats provider read and signed coordinate lookup. Provider/parse failures store a sanitized failure audit with no observation/outbox. Migration 427, exact worker DSN/credential/provider key, and its signed grant are not deployed; feature remains off. Existing persisted tasks remain mapped to the legacy module until schedule owners reconcile them.

scheduled_modules.scope: The scheduled contract requires one explicit --location-id; aggregate --all-locations is rejected. The query selects only active locations with coordinates and the CLI requires a scope before opening PostgreSQL.
scheduled_modules.idempotency: PostgreSQL upserts on (location_id, forecast_date, forecast_hour, source); the ClickHouse outbox uses a canonical payload hash. A retry refreshes matching forecast slots without creating duplicate natural-key rows.
scheduled_modules.retry_boundary: Legacy persisted tasks still use the shared runtime identity and remain allowlisted until schedule owners reconcile them. A retry repeats the OpenWeatherMap request and may update forecasts for the same location/window; the generated schedule remains disabled.

scheduled_modules.scope: The default-off worker requires one explicit --location-id, strips shared PostgreSQL identity settings from its child environment, and establishes a signed weather_forecast/ingest grant for the exact location before each database operation. Migration 426 exposes only signed coordinate lookup and a bounded atomic forecast/audit/outbox function; no direct application-table privileges are granted.
scheduled_modules.idempotency: PostgreSQL upserts on (location_id, forecast_date, forecast_hour, source); the canonical ClickHouse outbox uses a payload hash and rejects a conflicting reused key. Forecast rows, audit state, and outbox intent commit atomically.
scheduled_modules.retry_boundary: A retry repeats the provider request and signed location lookup, then revalidates the grant in the write transaction. Provider/parse errors produce a sanitized failed-ingestion audit row with no forecast or outbox rows. The feature remains off until migration 426 and a worker-specific grant/credential are provisioned; existing persisted tasks using the legacy module remain mapped separately until owner reconciliation.

scheduled_modules.scope: Global crop/commodity market data; optional commodity and period arguments filter the run.
external_effects: World Bank Pink Sheet HTTP download; explicit local reference seed mode
scheduled_modules.idempotency: Live World Bank observations use source=world_bank_pink_sheet; explicit reference samples use source=world_bank_pink_sheet_seed. Both use ON CONFLICT (source, commodity_code, market_name, price_date) DO NOTHING; historical corrections remain a separate policy question.
scheduled_modules.retry_boundary: Provider download, unusable/empty response, insert, and audit failures raise to the scheduler. Provider parsing completes before PostgreSQL opens, and each price batch plus its ingestion_log record commits atomically. The local seed source is never an implicit provider fallback.

scheduled_modules.scope: The direct indexer can process all active tracked wallets on configured chains unless --chain selects one chain. Kernel scheduled tasks require exactly one explicit supported --chain; the optional Prefect adapter preserves all three configured chains in Celo-first order.
scheduled_modules.idempotency: attestation_record uses attestation_uid conflict suppression; ClickHouse projection has an attestation UID key. Migration 421 stores a timestamp cursor per chain and tracked recipient; migration 422 resets inherited cursors to zero for a one-time full-history recovery. Each successful recipient's records, projection intents, and cursor advance commit together.
scheduled_modules.retry_boundary: A provider failure rolls back only that recipient, leaves its cursor unchanged, commits successful recipients, and returns a retryable command failure. The scan intentionally revisits the saved timestamp second; UID conflict suppression makes repeats idempotent. An outbox failure rolls back all current transaction state. Earlier-timestamp late arrivals and concurrent offset-page shifts still need provider/runtime reconciliation.

scheduled_modules.scope: The direct CLI can process all active tracked wallets unless chain or wallet address selects a narrower source. Kernel scheduled tasks require exactly one supported --chain, with an optional wallet filter; the optional Prefect adapter preserves the seven CLI-supported networks as separate scoped runs.
scheduled_modules.idempotency: wallet_activity_event suppresses duplicate transaction hashes; only inserted rows are projected under a stable outbox source key. Wallet activity, chain status, and projection intent commit together.
scheduled_modules.retry_boundary: One run owns a single PostgreSQL transaction with a savepoint per wallet. A provider or insert failure rolls back that wallet, marks its chain error, and permits successful wallet rows and outbox intents to commit. A status, outbox, or commit failure rolls back the run; the indexer then attempts to persist error status on the same connection. Retries repeat point-in-time RPC reads. This module does not scan transaction history or prove confirmation depth/reorg completeness.

scheduled_modules.scope: Manual capture modes retain their explicit location-bound inputs. Scheduled mode requires one canonical --location-id and one --driver-instance-id; the registry query accepts only an enabled sensor driver instance whose assigned location exactly matches the task. The loaded driver must be a code-installed sensor pull driver that explicitly opts in. The built-in sensor_csv pull driver reads its configured file path from the registered instance, never from task arguments, and is bounded to 100 sources/10,000 records. MQTT remains event-driven. This UUID scope does not authenticate the scheduler or establish tenant authorization/RLS.
external_effects: Filesystem read from the configured sensor_csv source path
scheduled_modules.idempotency: The batch writes canonical readings, ClickHouse outbox projections, ingestion audit, and new-reading events in one PostgreSQL transaction. Sensor timestamp uniqueness suppresses exact duplicate values and rejects conflicting values; duplicate rows do not publish another event. Source ordering and external file changes are not checkpointed.
scheduled_modules.retry_boundary: A failed database batch rolls back all accepted rows/projections/events; the driver instance status is updated separately. Replaying the same sensor timestamp/value is idempotent, while a conflicting timestamp fails the batch. Provider-file advancement and populated-source parity remain unverified.

scheduled_modules.scope: Configured Gnosis DAO/contracts and indexed protocol events; wallet ownership can resolve farm location rows.
scheduled_modules.idempotency: Migration 423 adds a transaction-hash/log-index receipt for newly processed event logs. An identical receipt is skipped before projections; a reused log identity with changed block hash, number, or event type fails closed. Receipt creation shares the transaction with governance/treasury/digital-lego projections, ClickHouse outbox intents, and the block checkpoint. Migration 424 gives the Moloch indexer its own status cursor; historical event rows are not backfilled because they lack log_index and block_hash.
scheduled_modules.retry_boundary: Each scanned block range and its chain_indexer_status checkpoint now commit on the same PostgreSQL connection; a failed range rolls back and stops the run, preserving the last committed boundary. Migration 424 seeds the dedicated gnosis_moloch cursor from the last shared (gnosis, rpc) boundary, marks it paused with provenance, and leaves the wallet-RPC row intact. The indexer rejects an inherited, unreviewed cursor unless the operator supplies --from-block; the first successfully committed range records that review. Removed-log rollback, deep reorg reconciliation, and historical receipt backfill must be resolved before automatic activation.

scheduled_modules.scope: Scheduled JobSpec execution requires one explicit --location-id; recent sensor readings and baseline rows are filtered to it, and cooldown/alert/ingestion-lineage operations retain that location. The hourly Prefect adapter fans out over active Kokonut Network locations. Scoped runs do not bootstrap shared alert-rule reference rows. Manual anomaly, baseline, and ML-check operations require --location-id or explicit --all-locations; no-argument invocation prints help. ML training requires one location, and --list-rules remains an explicit global read. The event handler is source-reading scoped.
external_effects: Scheduled CLI mode can send email and Directus notifications; event mode queues notifications durably. Actuation is recorded for later approval/execution in PostgreSQL; this module does not publish MQTT commands.
scheduled_modules.idempotency: The event handler reserves a per-source-reading/rule effect receipt and commits alert/claim/notification intent atomically. Scheduled window scans are now location-scoped but remain at-least-once; duplicate alert behavior across retries requires separate populated-data review. Actuation remains behind approval policy.
scheduled_modules.retry_boundary: The handler deduplicates same-reading/rule retries. Scheduled retries may repeat readings within the same location and the current code does not establish batch-window idempotency; direct external notification delivery remains at-least-once.

scheduled_modules.scope: Scheduled metric compute requires exactly one --location-id and uses --all or --metric; its --all-locations mode is rejected. NOI snapshot reconciliation has a separate default-off worker entrypoint and signed function boundary. The optional Prefect adapter fans out over active locations directly assigned to Kokonut Network.
scheduled_modules.idempotency: Each compute inserts a new metric_value with verified=false; repeated calculations are not deduplicated by the engine. Recalculation remains a draft write, never human verification.
scheduled_modules.retry_boundary: A scheduler retry may create another metric draft for the same location/period; human review state remains separate.

scheduled_modules.scope: Requires one canonical --location-id and the default-off KOKONUT_FEATURE_SIGNED_NOI_SNAPSHOT_WORKER gate. It opens only KOKONUT_NOI_SNAPSHOT_DATABASE_URL, establishes the exact signed noi_snapshot/reconcile grant, and calls migration 425; its child environment strips shared PostgreSQL login settings. The bounded function repeats the signed location predicate on both crop_cycle and v_crop_cycle_noi.
scheduled_modules.idempotency: Snapshots upsert by crop_cycle_id within the signed location. A conflicting existing snapshot assigned to a different location is left unchanged; retry refreshes the same location row.
scheduled_modules.retry_boundary: The function runs in the caller-owned worker transaction. Missing credentials, a revoked/expired grant, wrong resource/action, or a location mismatch fails before a snapshot write. No aggregate mode is accepted.

scheduled_modules.scope: --check scans configured sources and all locations unless --source narrows the configuration set.
scheduled_modules.idempotency: Alert state is locked per source/location and transitions use cooldown logic; every check and provider attempt is retained. End-to-end provider delivery is at-least-once.
scheduled_modules.retry_boundary: Database state is durable; external delivery needs receiver idempotency or operator reconciliation.

scheduled_modules.scope: All active dashboard_dataset definitions selected by the CLI; result source is limited to the three curated reporting views when the feature is explicitly enabled.
scheduled_modules.idempotency: Refresh writes only a row count and metadata. The current SQL text and active state are compared at update time to reject stale results.
scheduled_modules.retry_boundary: KOKONUT_FEATURE_LEGACY_DATASET_SQL defaults off; enabled reads use the separate ACL-verified read-only analytics role.

scheduled_modules.scope: Exactly one required --location-id per process; --all means all climate providers for that location, not all locations.
external_effects: ERA5 Land (--ncep), MODIS, SMAP, and Sentinel-1 requests through Google Earth Engine; the worldclim command makes no network request and records a latitude_proxy_v1 estimate
scheduled_modules.idempotency: worldclim_climate uses a partial unique key for one location-level row (plot_id IS NULL); migration 397 refuses duplicate legacy rows without deleting them. GEE summary tables have no matching unique key and provider retries may insert duplicates.
scheduled_modules.retry_boundary: Per-location retry is the intended unit; GEE writes commit before ingestion_log writes, so a crash can leave an unlogged provider row. The historical seed's --all argument is invalid because --location-id is required.

scheduled_modules.scope: --process and --event-worker claim the global event queue; --notification-process and --notification-worker claim the global notification outbox; --worker remains the combined compatibility mode. Event handlers may be tenant-scoped, global, or external as recorded below.
external_effects: Delegated to registered event handlers; --notification-process and --notification-worker may deliver email, webhook, or Directus notifications
scheduled_modules.idempotency: Per-event/per-handler receipts suppress already-successful handlers. Outbox enqueue uses stable source/channel/destination keys. Event and provider delivery remain at-least-once across lease expiry or a crash after an external effect.
scheduled_modules.retry_boundary: Event and notification queues use durable leases and bounded retries. Dead-letter replay/disposal and event cleanup are excluded from scheduled operation contracts; cleanup retention remains an owner decision.

scheduled_modules.scope: Dedicated scheduled entrypoint recomputes and reports potential adjustment differences for exactly one required --location-id. The CLI and scheduler contract reject an unscoped all-location scan; the interactive credit-management CLI is not scheduler-allowlisted.
scheduled_modules.idempotency: The check recomputes from current verified source rows inside a database-enforced read-only transaction; it does not write credit adjustments, retirement state, or review decisions. Repeating it has no database side effects.
scheduled_modules.retry_boundary: Retry repeats bounded database reads and reports current differences. The interactive issuance, adjustment, retirement, and retirement-review CLI is outside the scheduler module allowlist.

scheduled_modules.scope: Every CLI mode and due-job claim requires one explicit --location-id; job lookup, listing, job creation, and due-row leases are limited to that location. It processes at most --limit jobs sequentially (1-10; the shared JobSpec defaults to one). The optional Prefect adapter fans out over active Kokonut Network locations. Provider job rows must already be configured and active for execution; queue execution creates no jobs.
external_effects: ClickHouse projection delivery only through the separately optional outbox worker
scheduled_modules.idempotency: Due rows are claimed with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, filtered by the required location, and protected by one 30-minute lease at a time. remote_sensing_observation has a unique source_system/source_id key; provider attempts are append-only and can repeat across retries.
scheduled_modules.retry_boundary: The configured provider can fall back to the other supported provider. Retryable failure schedules the job for 15 minutes later; completion updates are lease-owner guarded. The process bounds each invocation and claims the next row only after the current provider attempt finishes.

scheduled_modules.scope: Global projection queue; the supported scheduled operation is --run-once with a bounded batch (the current JobSpec fixes --limit 100). Operator list, replay, disposal, and manual reconciliation commands are excluded from scheduled arguments.
external_effects: When ClickHouse is enabled, writes allowlisted projection rows to the optional ClickHouse provider; when disabled, leaves queue rows untouched.
scheduled_modules.idempotency: Stable event keys and payload hashes suppress duplicate enqueue; lease tokens guard completion. External ClickHouse delivery is at-least-once across a crash after the provider write and before PostgreSQL completion.
scheduled_modules.retry_boundary: Expired claims are recovered and delivery retries are bounded at eight attempts before dead-lettering; every batch is capped at 1000 rows and the scheduled JobSpec requests 100.

event_handlers.scope: One event/source reading and its location. The handler receives a dedicated sensor_anomaly database URL and credential through exact source-controlled routing, then establishes signed transaction context and uses bounded database functions through migrations 405-414. It has no shared-DSN fallback or direct access to protected source/effect tables.
event_handlers.idempotency: A signed per-reading/rule receipt fences the bounded effects; the handler commits its source, alert, audit, event, notification, and optional draft/actuation intents atomically before the parent worker stores its delivery receipt.
event_handlers.retry_boundary: The handler may run again after crash or lease expiry; its source-reading/rule effect receipt suppresses duplicate database effects, while notification delivery remains at-least-once.

event_handlers.scope: Global notification outbox operation. When KOKONUT_FEATURE_ISOLATED_NOTIFICATION_ENQUEUE is enabled, a separate login calls the migration-417 bounded function with function ACLs kept private by migrations 418-419 and actual runtime-role bootstrap; exact source event type and optional payload location lineage are rechecked in SQL. The value remains optional, non-authoritative notification lineage and grants no tenant access. The default-off compatibility path retains the shared runtime connection.
event_handlers.idempotency: The bounded function validates and inserts by stable source-event/channel/destination identity, returns zero on exact replay, fills only missing location lineage, and rejects changed payload/type/location content. Remote delivery remains at-least-once unless the receiver honors its idempotency key.
event_handlers.retry_boundary: Event retry repeats durable enqueue through the stable notification identity; the dedicated function cannot send messages or mutate delivery leases, attempts, or dead-letter state. Provider sending and operator replay remain separate outbox-worker operations.

event_handlers.scope: Requires the matching event ID and one canonical payload location; when signed cache invalidation is enabled, establishes computation_cache/invalidate worker context and the database function rechecks event type/location before touching that location's analytics rows. The default flag preserves the existing scoped runtime-cache path.
event_handlers.idempotency: Repeated invalidation of the same location is idempotent; concurrent and crash/retry evidence exists for this handler.
event_handlers.retry_boundary: Lease expiry or crash may invoke invalidation again; repeated location-scoped invalidation is safe and does not affect other locations.

event_handlers.scope: Requires the matching event ID and one canonical payload location; when signed cache invalidation is enabled, establishes computation_cache/invalidate worker context and the database function rechecks event type/location before touching that location's CRISP rows. The default flag preserves the existing scoped runtime-cache path.
event_handlers.idempotency: Repeated invalidation of the same location is idempotent; concurrency, timeout, lease takeover and crash/retry evidence exists for this handler.
event_handlers.retry_boundary: Lease expiry or crash may invoke invalidation again; repeated location-scoped invalidation is safe and does not affect other locations.

event_handlers.scope: Requires the matching durable event ID and canonical payload location; when signed cache invalidation is enabled, establishes computation_cache/invalidate worker context and migration 416 rechecks event type/location before invalidating only that location's metric rows. The default flag preserves the existing scoped runtime-cache path.
event_handlers.idempotency: Repeated location-scoped invalidation is idempotent; the four-handler disposable PostgreSQL acceptance verifies same-event retry returns zero additional invalidations.
event_handlers.retry_boundary: Lease expiry or crash may invoke invalidation again; repeating the location-scoped invalidation does not affect other locations.

The value remains optional, non-authoritative notification lineage and grants no tenant access. The default-off compatibility path retains the shared runtime connection.

known_open_items: Trace the transitive service/calculator/provider call graph for every scheduled command, including dynamic SQL and file/network effects.

Reconcile existing enabled scheduled_task rows and external scheduler definitions against the new operation contracts; invalid persisted rows fail before subprocess creation but are not automatically rewritten.

Provision worker database principals, credentials, and exact grants for remaining operations before their SQL can be trusted under RLS; NOI snapshot, anomaly, opt-in cache handler, and notification-enqueue integrations remain default-off and require credential provisioning and candidate rollout after disposable SQL acceptance.
Do not enable application RLS or narrow broad runtime DML grants until the complete call graph, external/operator schedules, and owner mappings are reconciled.
